blocks.text: Cloud Site Spawner — Wave 3: The Orchestration Wave

content.value: Turn a merged foundation into a WORKING feature: bp cloud site create -> deploy -> a live https URL serving real Barkpark content -> rollback in under a second, PROVEN live on guerrilla. Opened at STRATEGIZE 2026-07-14. IN FLIGHT NOW: SURVEYING — 18 Sonnet surveyors mapping the remote-exec seam, the engine contract, the token lifecycle, and the live-proof gates before Digest designs the verify fleet.

Make the site-spawner deploy PERFECT and actually WORKING end-to-end. Today the Wave-1 foundation is merged and live (Registry.Site/Deployment schema with kind=static + build_id/content_rev/stage, deploy/site-deploy.sh 6-stage engine with atomic symlink switch + instant rollback + a CI-gated --self-test, the Astro adapter, the static Caddy renderer, bp cloud site CLI verbs, and the PublicRead token clamp) — but the pieces are NOT wired server-side, so a spawn cannot actually happen: POST /v1/sites/:id/deploy refuses a content-bound static site with 422 no_build_source (router.ex:4687 requires artifact_url OR github_repo), and the CLI's deployment poll + rollback routes 404. Wire the spine and PROVE it: bp cloud site create -> deploy (walking the six visible stages PLAN->BUILD->STAGE->HEALTH->SWITCH->RETIRE) -> a live https URL serving the user's Barkpark content -> rollback in under a second — demonstrated LIVE on guerrilla, not just unit-tested. It must be beautiful: honest streamed stage status, real failure messages, a broken build never reaching visitors, and the box staying the origin.

blocks.title: The engine is not on main

content.value: Second reconciliation: the container deploy path in cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/web/router.ex:4680 enqueues a queued Deployment row for 'the off-box builder (P2)' which 'polls for queued rows'. That builder is remembered as NOT LIVE. So there is likely NO existing mechanism by which the control plane causes anything to execute on an instance box. That missing remote-exec seam — not the 422 — is the true crux of this wave, and survey question #1 exists to find or refute it.

blocks.text: Direction — the spine, the seam, and one live URL

content.value: This wave has exactly one job and it is not a checklist: make a spawn HAPPEN. The finished experience: a user types bp cloud site create my-blog --framework astro --kind static --dataset ws/proj/production, then bp cloud site deploy my-blog, and watches six honest stages tick by — PLAN (dedup on build_id), BUILD (npm install + astro build in a scrubbed, capped, flocked sandbox), STAGE (dist/ copied into an immutable releases/<build_id>/), HEALTH (a loopback server asserting the baked bp-build-id + bp-content-rev markers, not mere reachability), SWITCH (an atomic symlink rename), RETIRE (keep N=5) — and then a real https URL serves their real content. Then bp cloud site rollback flips the symlink back in under a second. When BUILD fails, the stream says WHY, in the user's words, and nothing switches: a broken build never meets a visitor.

The load-bearing choice I lean toward: the control plane ORCHESTRATES but the BOX EXECUTES. POST /v1/sites/:id/deploy kind-branches on static, computes build_id = hash(code_rev + content_rev + config), mints the deployment row, and returns 201 instantly; an async runner drives deploy/site-deploy.sh ON the site's box with a SCRUBBED env (only the injected BARKPARK_* vars + the read_token revealed from Vault — an ambient BARKPARK_TOKEN/URL silently shadows the per-site token because Vite gives process.env precedence over .env; this is live-proven, so the scrub is load-bearing), parsing the engine's stage lines and CASing them into the deployment's nullable stage + append-only console. The status enum stays at four (D3); the six stages ride telemetry. Rollback is kind-branched to site-deploy.sh --rollback (D5) — NEVER promotion_attrs.

The seam I do NOT yet know, and will not guess: HOW the control plane reaches the box. Three shapes are plausible — (a) SSH from Elixir over the key the provisioner already holds; (b) an on-box poller inside the instance's own Barkpark that claims queued static deployments and reports stages back (mirrors the self-update curator, mirrors the router's own 'off-box builder polls' comment, and is crash-safe by construction); (c) collapse the whole thing onto ONE box for the wave-3 proof and generalize later. I lean (b) if any polling substrate already exists, (a) if SSH is already how instances get commanded, and I will accept (c) ONLY if it does not fork the architecture. Survey decides; Decide finalizes. The one thing I will not accept is inventing a second, silent 'site' execution path.

Scope discipline. The finish line stays D4: PATH-under-existing-FQDN via a marker-guarded Caddy handle_path — no wildcard, no on_demand_tls (never run live), no DNS write. Beauty is IN scope, not polish-later: streamed stage status and honest failure copy are wish criteria. If it fits inside eight slices, the D18 Caddy TLSMode branch rides along; if it does not, it is backlog without apology. Deferred as before: SSR node slots, content-webhook auto-rebuild, non-Astro adapters, subdomain graduation.

Kinsta/Vercel. Judged holistically on one question: can a human, on guerrilla, go from nothing to a live URL serving their own content and back again in under a second — and did they enjoy watching it? If a slice cannot be PROVEN live this wave, the ledger says so honestly. A claimed green that was never earned is worse than an honest red.

blocks.text: The three ways this wave dies

content.value: 1. The remote-exec seam does not exist and we build a ghost. Mitigated by survey #1 and a verify pass with run-proof.
2. Nothing mints the per-site public-read token, so BUILD has no credential and cannot fetch content. Suspected hole; survey #5 hunts it.

3. The Caddy path-handle splice breaks the very vhost serving the content API on the box we are demoing. Survey #12 maps the backup/validate/reload-or-revert discipline before a single byte is written.
Width is cheap now and buys precise depth later. Every surveyor writes their findings to their OWN bp task; the Digest phase folds them back into this Paper.

Map every candidate: SSH from Elixir, the Hetzner client, the provisioner, cp-deploy.sh/instance-deploy.sh triggers, the self-update curator, any on-box agent that polls. Name the exact module+function that could run deploy/site-deploy.sh on guerrilla — or prove NONE exists and say what the cheapest honest seam would be.
Why: This is THE architectural crux: /v1/sites lives on the control plane, but site-deploy.sh must RUN on the box that holds the content. Everything else in the wave hangs off the answer.

RECONCILIATION THAT CHANGES THE WAVE: SLICE ZERO IS ALREADY DONE. The Strategize brief (and 13 of 17 surveyors, who read a stale checkout) said #3068 (site-deploy.sh) and #3071 (PublicRead mount) were still OPEN. They are not. Verified: #3068 MERGED 2026-07-14T08:01:04Z, #3071 08:01:09Z, #3130 08:01:13Z; origin/main is 51576f128; guerrilla (/opt/barkpark) is checked out at 51576f12, deploy/site-deploy.sh is on the box at -rwxr-xr-x 23589 bytes, and PublicRead appears twice in the box's api/lib/barkpark_web/router.ex. The auto-deploy on deploy/** and api/** did exactly what it was supposed to. There is no landing slice. The whole wave budget goes to orchestration + live proof.

PROCESS HAZARD, WAVE-WIDE: the primary checkout is ~25 commits BEHIND origin/main (local HEAD ba49148f3). Six independent surveyors were misled by it — reporting 'kind field does not exist', 'read_token_encrypted does not exist', 'templates/astro-starter is not in the tree'. Every one of those is a false negative. RULE FOR THIS WAVE: read via `git show origin/main:<path>` or build in a fresh worktree cut from origin/main. Never trust the working tree for site-spawner files.

THE SEAM EXISTS — and it is neither of the two the brief guessed. (a) SSH-from-Elixir: does NOT exist (grep -i ssh over cloud/lib and cloud/mix.lock = 0 hits; the only SSH is internal/cli/cloud/sshrunner.go, a provision-time operator CLI). (b) The on-box poller barkpark-agent IS live on every instance including guerrilla (systemd, 60s cycle, real os/exec, AgentToken auth) — but its wire Command is {ID,Name} with NO argv, its allowlist is exactly 6 fixed no-arg actions (internal/agent/commands.go:6-17,29-49, explicitly 'the security boundary'), and the server-side queue is a compile-time stub that ALWAYS returns [] (router.ex:8170-8173). It cannot carry a build_id. (c) THE REAL ONE, missed by the brief entirely: Registry.trigger_self_update/2 (cloud/lib/barkpark_cloud/registry.ex:2686-2702) does relay_admin_post(bp, "/v1/admin/self-update") — an authenticated HTTP POST from the control plane to the instance's own /v1/admin/* API, using a stored per-instance admin token, which the box then executes as a real OS process via Barkpark.SelfUpdate.Runner (Port-wrapped GenServer, fail-closed behind an apply flag). This is LIVE and proven for self-update AND rollback (isu-w6), and AutoupdateRolloutWorker drives the whole fleet through it. A /v1/admin/site-deploy sibling controller is the cheapest honest seam: same credential, same process model, zero new key management, and it is crash-safe the same way.

THE REAPER WILL SABOTAGE US. Registry.reap_stale_deployments/0 pass (0) (registry.ex:4551-4564) terminally fails ANY queued deployment whose artifact_url is nil AND whose site.github_repo is nil — with the message 'no build source'. That is the NORMAL, CORRECT shape of a static queued row. The query has no s.kind predicate. The moment we lift the 422, every static deploy gets killed by the next 1-minute Oban tick, mislabeled. This is worse than today's honest 422 and is easy to miss in a demo. It must be kind-scoped in the SAME slice that lifts the gate.

THE ENGINE HAS NO MACHINE STAGE PROTOCOL. site-deploy.sh's stdout is log prose with inconsistent per-prefix semantics: PLAN:/BUILD: announce BEFORE the work, STAGE:/SWITCH: log AFTER success, RETIRE emits ZERO lines when nothing is retired (the common case), and a SKIP_BUILD redeploy emits NEITHER a BUILD: nor a STAGE: line. An orchestrator that CASes `stage` off regexed stage words will silently stall on the first re-deploy. Its exit codes ARE clean and typed (0/2/10-16/21-24), and --rollback-preflight prints one clean KV line (TARGET_BUILD=<id>). Decide's fork: loose-parse with explicit per-prefix + silent-stage handling, OR add a uniform `STAGE=<NAME> STATUS=start|ok|fail` emission to the engine (now a follow-up PR, no longer a pre-merge amendment).

THE CREATE PATH SILENTLY DROPS THE CONTENT BINDING. cloudclient.SpawnSiteCreate sends JSON keys workspace/project/dataset (client.go:1193-1201). The router's put_site_content_binding/2 (router.ex:8247-8260) reads ONLY bootstrap_workspace/bootstrap_project/bootstrap_dataset and read_token. Unmatched keys are ignored without error. So `bp cloud site create` returns 201 today with a site that has NO content binding and NO read token — a ghost success, worse than a loud failure. AND: nothing anywhere MINTS the per-site public-read token (the server only encrypts a plaintext the caller supplies; the CLI has no ReadToken field at all). The reusable precedent is live in prod: internal/cli/vercel_cmd.go:544-572 vercelMintReadToken POSTs {label, permissions:["public-read"], dataset} to <scoped-base>/v1/tokens with an admin token. Also: barkpark_id is de-facto REQUIRED server-side (router.ex:4590) with no workspace-based fallback, while the CLI documents it as optional — omitting --instance 404s (mislabeled name_required).

THE CLI IS ALREADY AT THE KINSTA BAR AND IS WAITING FOR US. cloud_site_cmd.go's streamSiteDeploy (2s poll, 300-iteration cap, per-stage print-once dedup, canonical PLAN..RETIRE order with pending-fill, honest 'still in progress' on timeout, failure copy that names the stage AND says nothing switched) is merged and good. It 404s on two routes that do not exist: GET /v1/sites/:id/deployments/:dep_id (the poll) and POST /v1/sites/:id/rollback. The server is the entire gap. No CLI rework is needed for the MVP proof.

THE CADDY SPLICE IS DISCIPLINED BUT UNSERIALIZED. arm_caddy_site_route mirrors arm_caddy_mcp_route line-for-line (marker guard, anchor on the first `reverse_proxy localhost:(4000|4001)`, backup, awk-insert, `caddy validate`, reload-or-revert). Guerrilla's live Caddyfile DOES contain that anchor (verified by ssh), so the splice will find its slot. BUT: instance-deploy.sh holds a GLOBAL /var/lock/barkpark-instance-deploy.lock while it mutates the Caddyfile; site-deploy.sh holds a PER-SLUG lock that shares no namespace with it. Both do read → cp backup → awk to tmp → mv over live. Guerrilla auto-deploys on every merge. A site deploy racing an instance deploy can silently clobber the blue/green port flip and point Caddy at a slot that is about to be stopped — a live outage on the exact box we are demoing. Each writer is safe against ITSELF; none is safe against a third party. This needs one shared Caddyfile lock.

npm IS ON THE BOX BUT NOT ON THE PATH. Node 26.5.0 / npm 11.17.0 exist only via /root/.asdf/shims; a bare non-interactive exec has no asdf on PATH (which node fails). site-deploy.sh's BUILD scrub is `env -i PATH=$PATH ...` — it INHERITS the caller's PATH, it does not source asdf. Whatever invokes it must set PATH explicitly (api/start.sh already does exactly this for the BEAM). If the seam is the admin relay, the script runs as a child of the BEAM and inherits the BEAM's PATH — which start.sh already asdf-ified. That is a point IN FAVOUR of the relay seam, and it is verifiable.

THE DEMO HAS NO CONTENT. guerrilla's default/default/production dataset holds Barkpark's own dogfood schemas (task, paper, ticket, quiz, sheet, book, arena…). There is no `post` type (the Astro starter's default BARKPARK_DOC_TYPE) — GET /v1/data/query/production/post 404s — and every schema sampled has visibility UNSET, not "public", which the PublicRead clamp requires. The demo needs a seeded workspace/project/dataset with a public-visibility schema and one published document. Nobody has scripted this. It is a real slice, not a footnote.

SMALLER, SETTLED: the astro adapter bakes FIVE markers, not two (bp-build-id, bp-content-rev, bp-doc-id, bp-doc-title, bp-site-base) — HEALTH can assert content truth, not just build identity. The required BUILD env set is BARKPARK_API_URL + BARKPARK_DATASET (hard-required, throws), plus BARKPARK_TOKEN / BARKPARK_SITE_BASE / BARKPARK_BUILD_ID / BARKPARK_CONTENT_REV; omitting SITE_BASE silently defaults every site to /sites/astro-starter/. Deployment.promotion_attrs carries only git_ref+artifact_url — it cannot express a static rollback, confirming D5's kind-branch. FailureCopy.humanize/1 already has a 'no build source' clause worded for the container model that will now MISLEAD static sites. cloud/ has ZERO System.cmd today and zero Sobelow/Credo in CI (security.yml is api/**-scoped) — a router-reachable exec in cloud/ would be scanned by nothing. D18 (Caddy TLSMode) is confirmed READY, small, and additive: 4 golden tests should pass UNCHANGED if the zero-value default is byte-identical.

blocks.text: DECISIONS — D22 through D32 (the charter is the epic's memory; this is the wave's story)

content.value: D22 — THE REMOTE-EXEC SEAM IS THE ADMIN RELAY. The control plane reveals the instance's Vault-stored admin token and POSTs to the instance's own /v1/admin/site-deploy; the instance runs site-deploy.sh as a Port child of its own BEAM. WHY: it is the only seam that exists and is credentialed today (self-update rides it fleet-wide), it needs no new key management, and a BEAM child inherits asdf's npm for free.

D23 — A NEW Barkpark.Sites.DeployRunner, NOT SelfUpdate.Runner. WHY: the existing runner's command is compile-time config (it can never carry a build_id), its single-flight slot is global (guerrilla auto-deploys on every merge — a demo deploy would 409 against our own PR), and its 500-line log ring evicts the oldest lines, eating PLAN/BUILD under real npm output.

D24 — THE BUILD CHILD'S ENV IS PATH-PRESERVING AND KEY-REMOVING. WHY: the BEAM's env holds BARKPARK_KEK and BARKPARK_CLOAK_KEY and npm ci runs arbitrary postinstall code; Erlang's env option only ADDS/OVERRIDES, so removal requires {~c"VAR", false} — a naive allowlist silently leaks and passes review. And clearing PATH makes npm vanish.

D25 — THE ENGINE GAINS A MACHINE STAGE PROTOCOL (BPSTAGE name=… status=… build_id=…) at every boundary INCLUDING the silent ones. WHY: the two paths that emit nothing (PLAN no-op, SKIP_BUILD redeploy) are NORMAL, not exotic — a word-regexing orchestrator hangs on the first redeploy.

D26 — HEALTH ASSERTS MARKER VALUES, AND A HEALTH-FAILED BUILD IS PURGED. WHY: presence-only health let a lying build go live (proven), and the poisoned release dir makes a retry re-gate the same broken bytes forever.

D27 — ONE SHARED CADDYFILE LOCK across both deploy scripts. WHY: the lost-update race was reproduced and its consequence is a hard 502 on the content API of the demo box — and this wave's own merges fire the racing writer.

D28 — THE 422 LIFT AND THE REAPER KIND-SCOPE LAND IN THE SAME COMMIT, and both kinds still terminate. WHY: lifting the 422 alone kills every static deploy within 60 seconds under a false reason — invisible in a fast demo, and worse than today's honest refusal.

D29 — THE CONTROL PLANE MINTS THE READ TOKEN AT CREATE, over the scoped route, via a body-carrying relay — and the create path stops discarding the binding. WHY: without a credential the BUILD cannot fetch content, and the ghost 201 means the failure is silent.

D30 — THE SHIPPED CLI WIRE CONTRACT IS LAW; the server conforms. WHY: every mismatch (wrong envelope, wrong stage word, 200-with-ok:false) renders as a SILENT false success in front of a live audience, with the tests still green.

D31 — THE LIVE PROOF RUNS IN THE TEAM THAT OWNS GUERRILLA, against paper/task content with a PINNED doc id. WHY: the configured team owns zero barkparks (a cross-team create 404s before deploy is even reached), there is no `post` type, and the corpus shifts under concurrent sessions.

blocks.text: Direction — the spine, the seam, and one live URL

content.value: This wave has exactly one job and it is not a checklist: make a spawn HAPPEN. The finished experience: a user types bp cloud site create my-blog --framework astro --kind static --dataset ws/proj/production, then bp cloud site deploy my-blog, and watches six honest stages tick by — PLAN (dedup on build_id), BUILD (npm install + astro build in a scrubbed, capped, flocked sandbox), STAGE (dist/ copied into an immutable releases/<build_id>/), HEALTH (a loopback server asserting the baked bp-build-id + bp-content-rev markers, not mere reachability), SWITCH (an atomic symlink rename), RETIRE (keep N=5) — and then a real https URL serves their real content. Then bp cloud site rollback flips the symlink back in under a second. When BUILD fails, the stream says WHY, in the user's words, and nothing switches: a broken build never meets a visitor.

The load-bearing choice I lean toward: the control plane ORCHESTRATES but the BOX EXECUTES. POST /v1/sites/:id/deploy kind-branches on static, computes build_id = hash(code_rev + content_rev + config), mints the deployment row, and returns 201 instantly; an async runner drives deploy/site-deploy.sh ON the site's box with a SCRUBBED env (only the injected BARKPARK_* vars + the read_token revealed from Vault — an ambient BARKPARK_TOKEN/URL silently shadows the per-site token because Vite gives process.env precedence over .env; this is live-proven, so the scrub is load-bearing), parsing the engine's stage lines and CASing them into the deployment's nullable stage + append-only console. The status enum stays at four (D3); the six stages ride telemetry. Rollback is kind-branched to site-deploy.sh --rollback (D5) — NEVER promotion_attrs.

The seam I do NOT yet know, and will not guess: HOW the control plane reaches the box. Three shapes are plausible — (a) SSH from Elixir over the key the provisioner already holds; (b) an on-box poller inside the instance's own Barkpark that claims queued static deployments and reports stages back (mirrors the self-update curator, mirrors the router's own 'off-box builder polls' comment, and is crash-safe by construction); (c) collapse the whole thing onto ONE box for the wave-3 proof and generalize later. I lean (b) if any polling substrate already exists, (a) if SSH is already how instances get commanded, and I will accept (c) ONLY if it does not fork the architecture. Survey decides; Decide finalizes. The one thing I will not accept is inventing a second, silent 'site' execution path.

Scope discipline. The finish line stays D4: PATH-under-existing-FQDN via a marker-guarded Caddy handle_path — no wildcard, no on_demand_tls (never run live), no DNS write. Beauty is IN scope, not polish-later: streamed stage status and honest failure copy are wish criteria. If it fits inside eight slices, the D18 Caddy TLSMode branch rides along; if it does not, it is backlog without apology. Deferred as before: SSR node slots, content-webhook auto-rebuild, non-Astro adapters, subdomain graduation.

Kinsta/Vercel. Judged holistically on one question: can a human, on guerrilla, go from nothing to a live URL serving their own content and back again in under a second — and did they enjoy watching it? If a slice cannot be PROVEN live this wave, the ledger says so honestly. A claimed green that was never earned is worse than an honest red.

WHY: the BEAM's env holds BARKPARK_KEK and BARKPARK_CLOAK_KEY and npm ci runs arbitrary postinstall code; Erlang's env option only ADDS/OVERRIDES, so removal requires {~c"VAR", false} — a naive allowlist silently leaks and passes review. Self-review was exemplary — it named the flock-shim caveat and the CONTENT_REV seam rather than papering over them. Review CLOSED that seam: cloud sends content_rev -> the API sets it in the child env -> the engine cross-checks it. The conditional degradation the builder feared does not occur.

2. site-spawner-w3-admin-site-deploy-seam -> loop-epic/remote-exec-seam-post-get-v1-admin-site--1-r (+1 review commit). The seam is right: existing admin scope (zero new auth), a NEW per-slug DeployRunner (not SelfUpdate.Runner — its global slot would 409 against guerrilla's own post-merge self-update), stages retained outside the log ring, and a genuinely key-REMOVING env scrub ({~c"NAME", false} — an allow-list-SHAPED env: [...] reads like a scrub and still hands BARKPARK_KEK to npm's postinstall). REVIEW FIX: the engine emits the real failure reason as detail="…" on every terminal stage line, and the runner's regex DROPPED it — so npm's 401 and HEALTH's marker miss never reached the user, and every failure degraded silently to a canned line. Gate: 44 tests (+3), 0 failures.

3. site-spawner-backlog-server-orchestration -> loop-epic/control-plane-spine-kind-branch-the-depl-2-r (+2 review commits). The biggest slice and the one that makes a spawn possible. The reaper kind-scope landed in the SAME COMMIT as the 422 lift (a legitimate static row matches the container predicate EXACTLY — lifting alone would have terminally failed every static deploy within 60s, mislabelled); the read token is minted server-side at create over the SCOPED route; the two missing CLI routes exist in the CLI's exact shape. THREE REVIEW FIXES, two of them severe: (a) a FAILED box run settled as LIVE — the box reports `state: "done"` as a run LIFECYCLE and the control plane read it as a VERDICT, so a build dying at BUILD/HEALTH flipped current_deployment_id and printed a success URL (the health gate held, so visitors were safe — but the story we told about it was false); (b) ROLLBACK never waited for the flip (see the D22 correction above); (c) the ghost 201 had a second door — a static site with no content binding still inserted, then died to the reaper 60s later advising a flag the user could no longer use. Gate: 77 tests (+10), 0 failures; full cloud suite 1945/0.

4. site-spawner-w3-cli-honesty -> loop-epic/cli-honesty-instance-required-the-false--3-r (+1 review commit). --instance required client-side before any network call; the false 'the server resolves the instance from the workspace' comment deleted; `cancelled` terminal (it used to poll 300x2s and then print 'deploy in progress'); per-stage detail surfaced. Protective-verified by the builder (reverting the fix reproduces the exact original symptom). REVIEW FIX: cloudError read only `error` and DISCARDED `detail` — so the cloud slice's careful failure copy (which box refused, what it said, which flag fixes it) landed on screen as a bare machine slug. The two slices were talking past each other. Gate green.

5. cf-origin-ca-caddy-tls -> loop-epic/caddy-tlsmode-additive-tlsmode-certpath--4-r (+1 review commit). Purely additive TLSMode; all four pre-existing goldens pass with an EMPTY diff, which is machine-proof that the zero value is byte-identical. The builder generalized safeRoot -> safeCaddyPath rather than copy-pasting a third predicate (correct — a copy could only drift). REVIEW ADDITION: the builder's own biggest doubt was that a syntax error in the GLOBAL `servers { trusted_proxies … }` block would not degrade the CF sites but would fail the WHOLE config to load and wedge EVERY site on the box — and that a string test stays green through exactly that. So the render is now handed to a REAL caddy binary (`caddy validate`, three boxes incl. the untouched default). caddy v2.11.4 ACCEPTS it. The doubt is refuted, not merely documented. Gate green.

6. site-spawner-w3-live-proof -> loop-epic/the-live-proof-an-executable-create-depl-5 (UNCHANGED by review). The slice did the honest thing: it delivered a real proof harness and REFUSED to fabricate a green. deploy/site-spawner-live-proof.sh (730 lines) asserts BY VALUE, never by reachability, and splits fetching from judging so --self-check drives all 22 named reds OFFLINE and proves each one FIRES. Gate: bash -n clean, shellcheck clean, self-check 22/22. But see 'What stalled' — it has never run against a box.

blocks.text: WHAT STALLED — and it is the thing that matters

content.value: THE WISH IS NOT MET. The wish says 'demonstrated LIVE on guerrilla, not just unit-tested.' No live spawn has happened. Everything in this wave is proven against tests and fakes; the one artifact built to prove it for real stops before it creates anything.

THE HUMAN GATE (not a code defect). The live proof stops at PREFLIGHT_NO_BARKPARK (exit 32): the configured cloud session's team owns ZERO barkparks, and guerrilla's row belongs to team `guerrilla`. A cross-team create returns 404 barkpark_not_found (existence is not leaked across teams). The builder declined to adopt guerrilla via the worker-gated POST /v1/internal/barkparks — correct: that re-parents a live production box and no one gave that mandate. Re-verified at review with a freshly-built bp: the wall is real, and the content wall PASSES in both directions (type `paper` -> 1 published doc, pinned; type `post` -> exit 33, catching the D31 trap where an undefined type answers 200 count:0 and the build ships a silently EMPTY page).

TWO MISSING SERVER-SIDE LEVERS (filed at review; both are real product gaps, not just test scaffolding). (a) site-spawner-deploy-force-rebuild (P1): build_id = hash(code_rev|content_rev|config) and enqueue/2 returns {:duplicate, existing} for unchanged content, with NO override — so the proof cannot mint a SECOND build, and rollback has nothing to flip from. Step 4 would red against a perfectly correct engine. It also means a user who fixed something outside their content cannot re-run a deploy at all; 'deploy again to retry' is advice the API cannot honour. (b) site-spawner-site-rebind-content (P2): a site's dataset binding is immutable (no PATCH route, and no DELETE either), so there is no SERVER-SIDE way to poison a build — the builder's step-5 poison sets BARKPARK_DOC_TYPE as a LOCAL env var, but the build runs server-side with its env injected from the STORED binding, so it almost certainly never arrives. The builder named this himself rather than letting it read as proven.

blocks.text: THE PATTERN — the one lesson this wave should teach the epic

content.value: Five of the six slices were green in isolation. EVERY defect review found was at a seam between two slices, and every one was a false green rather than a crash: a failed build reported as live; a rollback that returned before the flip; the real failure reason parsed by nobody; the server's failure copy discarded by the client; a ghost row admitted at the door. In each case both sides' tests passed — against each side's OWN fake. FakeBoxRelay's default rollback reply ({"status":"rolled_back"}, synchronous, no build_id) is a shape the real box never sends, and three green tests rested on it. RULE FOR THE NEXT FAN-OUT WAVE: when two slices define a contract, at least ONE test must run against the REAL sibling — or the wave ships two mutually-consistent fictions.

FIXED — a surviving false-done on site-spawner-w3-live-proof. Criterion [1] ('LIVE: bp cloud site create on guerrilla returns 201 with content_bound=true') was marked MET, carrying evidence that actually proves criterion [0] (the script is bash -n / shellcheck clean). No site was ever created on guerrilla — the builder's own report and GET /v1/sites -> {"sites":[]} confirm it. The stamp landed one row late (bp task stamp --criterion is ZERO-based while every board renders 1..N — the wave's most-hit footgun, already filed as bp-task-stamp-criterion-index-is-zero-based-footgun). Repaired: [0] -> met with the evidence I re-verified myself, [1] -> un-flipped with a dated note naming the human gate.

FIXED — two tasks (site-spawner-w3-cli-honesty, cf-origin-ca-caddy-tls) had lifecycle `open` with no claim: their leases had lapsed, so the board read finished work as unstarted. Both set to in_progress and re-published.

CLEAN — every one of the six merge-gated criteria is correctly UNMET; the lead closes those on merge. Five of six builders hit the zero-based stamp footgun, caught it by reading the ledger back, and repaired it themselves — the one that survived is the one fixed above. No task outside this wave was touched. Backlog filed at review: site-spawner-deploy-force-rebuild (P1), site-spawner-site-rebind-content (P2), joining the seven the builders filed.

THE LIVE PROOF, AND NOTHING ELSE UNTIL IT IS GREEN. (1) Clear the barkpark-ownership human gate — a cloud session in the team that owns guerrilla, or a deliberate, mandated adoption. (2) Land site-spawner-deploy-force-rebuild (P1) and site-spawner-site-rebind-content (P2) — without them steps 4 and 5 CANNOT go green even with credentials. (3) Run deploy/site-spawner-live-proof.sh against guerrilla until it exits 0, and expect to rewrite step 5's poison. (4) Land site-spawner-backlog-site-teardown — there is no DELETE /v1/sites/:id, so the moment the proof goes green it leaks a site row + read token + releases dir + Caddy block on EVERY run, and a gate you cannot run twice is not a gate. Resist new surface. The spine is built; it has simply never been switched on.

STATUS: STRATEGIZE done. SURVEY done (18 reports). DIGEST done. VERIFY done (9 reports). DECIDE done (D22-D32). BUILD done (6/6 green). REVIEW done — this section. WAVE CLOSED at grade B+. The epic's next wave is a LIVE-PROOF wave, not a feature wave.
